summary: Account-level routing tag misassignment causes subset of APAC traffic to be served from EU pools leading to p99 inference spikes
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10T02:10:00Z, CartaLabs reported intermittent but sustained p95/p99 latency spikes (text-generation requests) for users in APAC. Affected requests repeatedly showed server-side processing time >1.5s above baseline and occasional client-observed timeouts. Impact: Customer-facing production traffic for CartaLabs (enterprise tier) experienced elevated tail latency and ~0.3% increase in 5xx/timeout errors across their routes. Environment: prod, customers in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) hitting Redwood hosted API with model redwood-7b pinned. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send generation request to /v1/generate with model redwood-7b from an APAC endpoint with account token for account id 0x7f9c. 2) Observe p99 latency using load with 1rps per user; 3) Compare backend route in request trace header x-rl-route. Observed behavior: Traces show APAC request path selecting eu-west-1 serving pool (route tag eu-dedicated-12) and an additional ~120-180ms RTT on top of normal processing. Expected behavior: APAC requests should route to ap-south-1 or nearest APAC pop. Initial logs/traces: - trace_id=trc-9a2b3c, route=eu-dedicated-12, start=2026-03-10T02:09:58Z, serving_latency_ms=432, network_rtt_ms=140 - auth: account_tag=acct:region:ap; route_decision: matched route by tag regex (regex_v2) - control-plane change: config-deploy id cfg-2026-03-10-02:05 replaced account routing ruleset with updated regex_v2 (see PR #421) Notes: Customer supplied sample request id andClientRequestId header. They reported that the issue started exactly after 02:05 UTC.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:25 - Maya Alvarez (Support): Raised with SRE after receiving customer report; initial hypothesis is routing misclassification. Adding Devon for routing/control-plane triage.

2026-03-10 02:37 - Devon Turner (SRE): Confirmed traces showing APAC-origin requests being admitted to eu-west pool. Control-plane change cfg-2026-03-10-02:05 touched account-routing regex. Rolling back to previous ruleset to test impact.

2026-03-10 02:42 - Elena Park (Engineering, control-plane): Rolled back cfg-2026-03-10-02:05 at 02:40 UTC; monitoring effect. Noted intermediate config introduced a greedy capture group that matched 'acct:region:ap' as 'eu' in some tag permutations.

2026-03-10 03:05 - CartaLabs (Customer): Confirmed observed latency drop on their side; p99 returned to expected baseline. Customer appreciates quick response; asked for root cause and mitigation steps.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Devon Turner (SRE): Follow-up: Re-ran canary with corrected regex and strict unit tests. Deployed cfg-2026-03-11-08:55 with patch. Added route-selection telemetry to flag cross-region hops in realtime.
2026-03-12 14:40 - Maya Alvarez (Support): Closing note to customer with rollback summary and follow-up actions scheduled. Customer acknowledged and closed on their side.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: New regex_v2 in control-plane mis-parsed account tags that include a feature-flag suffix (e.g., acct:region:ap+opt) causing false-positive match to EU route labels.
Hypothesis 2: Route weighting code change + regex caused deterministic tie-break to prefer eu-dedicated pools for certain account IDs during config rollout window.

Findings: - Replayed routing decision logs show 'matched_by=regex_v2' for affected account ids. - Example bad match: 'acct:region:ap+edge' matched pattern '(.*)eu(.*)' due to unanchored group introduced in PR 421. - No evidence of network path MTU issues or BGP flaps; network RTTs consistent with cross-region endpoints.
Telemetry: Added immediate metric 'cross_region_routing_by_account' and alert threshold for >0.1% cross-region route ratio. Historical scan found 0.02% baseline, spike to 0.8% during incident window.
Customer impact mapping: 72% of affected requests for CartaLabs hit eu-west due to their token tags containing legacy suffixes; other customers unaffected but similar tags could trigger issue.

Root cause: Unanchored regex and regression in control-plane route selection logic introduced in cfg-2026-03-10-02:05 (PR #421) caused certain account_tag permutations to match EU route rules instead of APAC-local rules during config rollout.
Contributing factor: No automated unit test coverage for tag permutations and missing canary guard for route-selection metrics during config deploys.
Mitigation attempted: Rollback to prior ruleset (02:40 UTC) which immediately reduced cross-region matches for affected accounts and restored normal p99 latency for CartaLabs.
resolution_notes: Immediate remediation: Rolled back cfg-2026-03-10-02:05 at 02:40 UTC; customer observed latency return to baseline within 20 minutes.
Permanent fix: Updated routing regex to use anchored patterns and added explicit negative lookups for legacy suffixes. Deployed corrected cfg-2026-03-11-08:55 after unit + canary tests.
Monitoring and alerts: Implemented 'cross_region_routing_by_account' metric and alert. Added a short-term dashboard for all enterprise customers to detect routing anomalies.

Process changes: - Require regex-heavy control-plane changes to include permutation test cases. - Add canary gating that monitors cross-region hop rate and auto-rolls back if threshold exceeded during initial rollout.

Customer communication: Sent summary to CartaLabs on 2026-03-11 with timeline, root cause analysis, and planned safeguards. Customer confirmed no further regressions and closed the ticket on their end.

Follow-ups (owners): - INT-4987 (Eng): Expand unit tests for routing rules (owner: Elena Park). - SRE playbook update (owner: Devon Turner) to include immediate mitigation steps for routing misclassification.
Status: Resolved and mitigations implemented; scheduled postmortem doc published to Confluence.
